notes: Work. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I'm enjoying the evening course.

B.source: I'm not enjoying the evening course.

notes: Education (adult). Default: affirmative.

A.source: The wifi isn't working in the kitchen.

B.source: The wifi is working in the kitchen.

notes: Tech/home. Same frame as r2pol-044; shared construction cluster (verifier VR-11). Default: affirmative.

A.source: I want the window seat on the train.

B.source: I don't want the window seat on the train.

notes: Travel/sensory preference. 'I want X' = speaker agent (CB-6). Default: affirmative.

A.source: I don't need to bring ID on Thursday.

B.source: I need to bring ID on Thursday.

notes: Civic/admin (e.g. voting). Negated modal. Default: affirmative.

A.source: My sister got the flat near the park.

B.source: My sister didn't get the flat near the park.

notes: Family/housing. Default: affirmative.

A.source: The gym class isn't running this week.

B.source: The gym class is running this week.

notes: Fitness. Inanimate subject = third party. Default: affirmative.

A.source: Wake me up early tomorrow.

B.source: Don't wake me up early tomorrow.

notes: Daily routine instruction. Both natural. [LATER] removed: imperatives carry no time chip (verifier VR-12). Default: affirmative imperative, likely with please.

A.source: Don't tell Sam about the leaving party.

B.source: Tell Sam about the leaving party.

notes: Work/social. Default: affirmative imperative.

A.source: Put the plants outside tonight.

B.source: Don't put the plants outside tonight.

notes: Gardening. Context 'Frost is forecast.' removed: it favoured the negated reading on every channel (verifier VR-13). Default: affirmative imperative.

A.source: The landlord didn't fix the boiler on Friday.

B.source: The landlord fixed the boiler on Friday.

notes: Housing. Default: affirmative.

A.source: My knee hurts on the stairs.

B.source: My knee doesn't hurt on the stairs.

notes: Health. Body part = speaker (CB-4). Default: affirmative.

A.source: We don't have enough chairs for the garden.

B.source: We have enough chairs for the garden.

notes: Hosting. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I can read the print on this label.

B.source: I can't read the print on this label.

notes: Vision/access. Noncritical 'small' replaced by 'label' (verifier VR-14: 'small print' is hard to read by definition). Default: affirmative; the negated report is the access need.

A.source: The airport bus doesn't stop near the hotel.

B.source: The airport bus stops near the hotel.

notes: Travel. Default: affirmative or a question.

A.source: I renewed the car insurance.

B.source: I didn't renew the car insurance.

notes: Money/admin. Default: affirmative.

A.source: The jazz concert didn't sell out.

B.source: The jazz concert sold out.

notes: Music. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I remember the password for the laptop.

B.source: I don't remember the password for the laptop.

notes: Tech. Default: affirmative.

context: Someone rang the bell while you were alone.

A.source: I didn't recognise the man at the front door.

B.source: I recognised the man at the front door.

notes: Home safety. Default: affirmative.

A.source: The chicken curry has dairy in it.

B.source: The chicken curry doesn't have dairy in it.

notes: Food/allergy; safety-relevant. Default: affirmative or a question.

A.source: I don't agree with the budget plan.

B.source: I agree with the budget plan.

notes: Work/meetings; dissent is the minority reading that must survive. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I told the night nurse I wasn't in pain.

B.source: I told the night nurse I was in pain.

notes: Negation only in the embedded clause; main clause affirmative. Codebook counts negation of what the main clause directly embeds as negated. Health; safety-relevant. Default: affirmative.

A.source: The doctor said the knee scan was clear.

B.source: The doctor said the knee scan wasn't clear.

notes: Embedded negation under a reporting verb. No agent chip: reporter (doctor) vs embedded subject (scan) is contestable, so agent is unscored. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I don't have any cash for the parking meter.

B.source: I have some cash for the parking meter.

notes: Negative-polarity item: A takes 'any', B takes 'some' (function words forced by polarity; not content words). Default: affirmative.

A.source: My partner is coming to the dinner too.

B.source: My partner isn't coming to the dinner either.

notes: Polarity-sensitive additive: 'too' vs NPI 'either'. Default: affirmative.

A.source: Nobody called about the flat viewing.

B.source: Somebody called about the flat viewing.

notes: Negative quantifier subject (nobody) instead of 'not'. No agent chip (nobody/somebody: doer unnamed). Default: affirmative.

A.source: There's oat milk in the fridge.

B.source: There's no oat milk in the fridge.

notes: Determiner negation 'no' in an existential (dummy 'there', so no agent chip). Default: affirmative.

A.source: Isn't the museum free on Sundays?

B.source: Is the museum free on Sundays?

notes: Negative yes/no question (positively biased, but negated on the words, which is what the codebook labels). Speech act question in both. Default: affirmative question.

A.source: I drive at night in winter.

B.source: I never drive at night in winter.

notes: Frequency negator 'never' on a habitual. Default: affirmative.

A.source: I don't have to wait in the hotel lobby.

B.source: I have to wait in the hotel lobby.

notes: Negated obligation ('don't have to' = no obligation, not prohibition). Speaker subject chosen to avoid the CB-1 directive reading of 'You have to'. Default: affirmative.

A.source: Leave the garden gate open.

B.source: Never leave the garden gate open.

notes: Prohibition with 'never' instead of 'don't'. Default: affirmative imperative.
